The Pacta Conventa is an agreement between Hungary and Croatia that was signed in the 11th century. The document established the personal union between the two kingdoms, and in exchange for Croatian loyalty we guaranteed their nobility exemption from taxes, the ability to maintain an independent viceroy and certain other political rights. This agreement is what has constrained our rule over Croatia for so long, while we have finally merged the kingdoms into one nation, the Pacta Conventa still stops us from having a unified political body to represent Hungarians and Croatians alike. With the support of the liberals we can modify the agreement to protect lesser rights of all Croatians, instead of protecting major rights of the nobility. This way, the commoners will love the new order of things and see themselves as willing citizens of Hungary!

The Supplex Libellus Valachorum is the name of a petition that was submitted by the Romanians of Transylvania to the Hungarian diet during the Grand German Revolt. The petition demanded equal rights for Romanians and ascencion to the national diet in Budepest. The petition was denied at the time, but after the outbreak of nationalism across Europa the king now sees it as beneficial to quell any potential secessionist movements. By signing the petition we will be forced to listen to "Romanian" "people" but in exchange we will get a steady supply of bodies to grind against the Bohemian and Polish armies should they dare invade us.

The Unio Trium Nationum was originally the name of a political alliance between different feudal estates against the Transylvanian peasantry, but over time it has taken on the colloquial meaning of the union between Hungary, Croatia and Romania against Greek influence. The political alliance has worked well, but now that we have united the 3 political entities as one nation, we are left with a "Unio Unius Nationis" which is not as menacing.
